seal.statement: Starting from the independently verified phases-1-through-5 raft-rs integration at fe6e04c3d, replace the rejected public Raft/node/control object boundary with an operation-only partition port. Callers may invoke measured semantic operations and read immutable snapshots by value, but cannot obtain or traverse a RawNode, raft-rs facade, handle, runtime host, group object, lifecycle decision input, durable lifecycle record, SQLite connection, mutable lifecycle state, or provider control. One private runtime owner is the sole production importer and invoker of the raft-rs binding; every actual core entry is counted at that lowest common invocation boundary and follows the private durable lifecycle eligibility owner. One lifecycle owner is the sole production writer of durable replica retirement, lifecycle administration is a separate command surface, and partitionControlOf or any replacement control accessor is absent. Logical retirement, group/runtime health, and host-operation failure remain independent; provenance is constructed as host preparation, private core result, then host persistence/send/apply. A host failure during an in-progress Ready cycle marks only that group recovery-required, and no subsequent operation enters its stale RawNode before reconstruction from coherent durable state. Persistence, send, address-resolution, and application failures each prove reconstruction under the same logical replica and peer identity without retirement or shared-runtime poisoning; a genuine core fatal likewise preserves logical identity across runtime reconstruction. Retirement remains terminal across restart even when stale ConfState contains self: every public active operation refuses before core entry, the core-entry count stays zero, no messages or term disturbance occur, and a deliberate lifecycle-owner bypass restores the old disruptive behavior. The real SQLite transaction boundary proves application effects and durable applied progress cannot split. A mechanical before/after inventory must show that the redesign removes more public capability than it adds, and transport remains blocked until an independent verifier approves the structural boundary.

text: Design vet round 1: REJECT, category-complete. The direction is sound, but the design does not yet prove the three structural questions. Import ownership scans only src/raft direct imports and misses re-exports, dynamic loads, facade-taking helpers and other src modules; retirement ownership scans one method spelling and misses direct SQL/aliases/store database exposure; the counter test is textual rather than a behavioral lowest-level instrument. Ready recovery lacks per-group serialization, a generation/CAS swap, async send awaiting, and a rule forbidding free/other entry on the stale handle. The exact partition operation contract, provider retention prohibition, authorized retirement owner/call path, message-group/createNodeClass disposition, typed reason/recovery table, explicit active|retired|missing|unreadable durable lifecycle state, retirement/core-entry linearization, immutable function/outcome surfaces, durable identity tuple registration, restart-vs-recovery reconstruction discriminator, application/progress transaction composition, mechanical eight-category capability ledger, three required mutants, and coupledPairs witnesses must be designed before implementation. Harness findings: one red control failed only because a future file was absent; function properties were not inspected; forbidden-name regexes repeated the rejected property-name pattern; four receipt files do not exist; the application fixture is an array rather than real SQLite. Evidence: subagent design report against cd7a09368 and paths cited in the report.

Design-verification scope expands to admission-gating, recovery-replay, concurrency-serialization, transport-delivery, harness-fidelity, and owner-interaction. The runtime/lifecycle, runtime/application-transaction, and partition/operation-port coupled boundaries require registered coupledPairs with deterministic witnesses before landing.

Strengthened the rejected initial design before production implementation: fixed the exact frozen operation contract; made the provider stateless; specified explicit active/retired identity rows and per-identity lifecycle/core linearization; added per-group serialization, generation-checked single-flight reconstruction, awaited delivery, no stale-handle free/entry, immutable typed provenance, a real SQLite application/progress transaction, repository-wide AST ownership audits, three controlled mutants, a pinned eight-category capability baseline, and non-vacuous red tests for every receipt.

Design vet round 2: REJECT. The amended architecture is materially stronger, but its proof plan still cannot establish the three stopping questions. Required changes: a reusable whole-src AST/dependency audit executed against mutated source copies for binding import/invocation, facade escape and lifecycle writer bypass; a counter observer that remains valid after the graph is removed; exact deep-frozen port/result/event whitelists and mechanically generated eight-category ledgers; executable retirement/restart, Ready phase, provenance, atomic SQLite and phase-regression witnesses; shared-runtime epoch fencing and a two-group await/trap replacement race; bounded stale-handle reclamation without entering quarantined handles; canonical classifyTransportDeliveryOutcome handling with noHandler/deferred/rejection/timeout and the existing delivery budget; a named lifecycle coordinator with identity administration off the data-plane port; both application/progress seams composed through one typed transaction interaction; and three registered coupledPairs with same-witness controls.

Closed round-2 design gaps before production work: removed identity mutation from the data-plane port; named replica removal execution as lifecycle coordinator; made every lease re-read durable lifecycle state; specified immutable observer-only core-entry telemetry; globally serialized complete operations and healthy runtime replacement so no cross-group trap can race an awaited Ready; named MessageRouter.messageTimeoutMs, resolveRaftTransportDeliveryOptions and classifyTransportDeliveryOutcome including noHandler/deferred/timeout semantics; specified whole-runtime generation replacement as bounded stale-handle reclamation; replaced the hand inventory with a reproducible eight-category generator; implemented a whole-src binding/lifecycle audit exercised against mutated source trees; specified exact deep-frozen port/event/result whitelists, real SQLite phase faults across both apply seams, a two-group race, timer/close races, three exact coupledPairs and the phase-1-through-5 evidence command.

Design vet round 3: REJECT on six architectural/proof-plan blockers only. A runtime-wide FIFO held across external awaits can deadlock reciprocal or local delivery; replace it with per-group serialization, short core-entry critical sections, runtime epochs and post-await fencing. Ready snapshot/entry-suffix/hard-state persistence also needs one durable transaction with delete/insert fault witnesses. Make lifecycleOwner.execute(identity, semanticCommand) the sole non-bypassable call path, including sole explicit-active creation. Strengthen the audit against aliases, computed calls, re-exports, dynamic/binding artifact imports and assembled lifecycle SQL rather than receiver-name heuristics. Define a separate operation-only membership identity administration owner with CAS and join/restart/address-resolution witness. Finally specify and drive retirement behavior for scheduling, subscription and close as well as direct core operations.

Resolved round-3 design blockers: replaced the across-await runtime FIFO with per-group queues, enqueue-and-ack inbound step, short lifecycle/runtime critical sections, active-epoch counters, post-await generation fencing and exclusive zero-active replacement; specified reciprocal/local reentrancy and trap-during-host-work liveness witnesses; made Ready snapshot, entry-suffix delete/inserts, HardState and commit point one SQLite transaction with reopen faults at every boundary; made lifecycleOwner.execute the only internal dispatcher caller and sole active-row creator; folded the binding loader into runtime owner and expanded the conservative audit/mutant requirements; defined a separate CAS membership-identity administration port and join/restart/address witness; and specified all eleven port operations under terminal retirement, including timer cancellation, passive subscription and close with zero core entry.

Design-admission round 4: APPROVE, limited to the six prior blockers. Per-group queues plus short runtime critical sections, enqueue-only inbound acknowledgement and runtime epochs remove across-await lock cycles; Ready persistence is one SQLite transaction with boundary faults; the only call graph is port to lifecycleOwner.execute closed command union to captured runtime dispatcher; the final audit is required to be conservative with individually asserted evasion mutants; peer identity reservation has a separate frozen CAS administration port and sole importer; and terminal-retirement semantics enumerate all eleven public operations with zero actual core entry. Implementation and final evidence still require independent verification.

Implementation discovery: the initial eleven-operation census hid one pre-existing learner-promotion semantic behind LifeRaft internals. Progress proof reads backend-owned follower match progress and, when absent/behind, asks Raft to materialize progress once. The boundary now exposes probePeerProgress(peerAddress) as the twelfth frozen semantic operation instead of exposing log/appendPacket/message; raft-rs projects its native Progress tracker through readStatus().followerProgress and LifeRaft keeps the former last-entry resend inside its adapter. The sealed quest statement and receipt set are unchanged; exact-surface and retirement tests enumerate the twelfth operation.
